claims.text: Large language models (LLMs) struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty.
LLMs are systematically overconfident when constructing confidence intervals around their own answers.
Nominal 99% confidence intervals from several modern LLMs cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
A conformal prediction based approach obtains accurate 99% observed coverage.
The Winkler interval score decreases by 54% with a conformal prediction based approach.
Direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment methods further reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.
LLMs exhibit overconfidence because when reasoning under uncertainty, they act as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution, neglecting its tails.

evidence.description: Large language models (LLMs) excel at numerical estimation but struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty.
We study how well LLMs construct confidence intervals around their own answers and find that they are systematically overconfident.
Across several modern models, nominal 99% intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
With a conformal prediction based approach that adjusts the intervals, we obtain accurate 99% observed coverage
and the Winkler interval score decreases by 54%.
We also propose direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment methods, which further reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.

Finally, we develop a perception-tunnel theory explaining why LLMs exhibit overconfidence: when reasoning under uncertainty, they act as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution, neglecting its tails.

methodologies.name: FermiEval
methodologies.description: A benchmark of Fermi-style estimation questions with a rigorous scoring rule for confidence interval coverage and sharpness.

methodologies.name: Conformal prediction based approach
methodologies.description: An approach that adjusts confidence intervals to obtain accurate coverage.

methodologies.name: Direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment
